text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Alija Izetbegovic, chairman of the Bosnian presidency, says in an interview that power is important and that all parties are fighting for power, but he says the main goal of his four-party coalition is to preserve Bosnia -- not power.

- The United States intends to be involved in Bosnia and this region on the long term to ensure successful implementation of the Dayton peace treaty, U.S. envoy Robert Gelbard says on arrival in Sarajevo.

- A session of the Bosnian council of ministers scheduled for Tuesday did not take place due to the absence of Serb representatives. The session was supposed to discuss the "quick start package" of economic reforms.
- Uncooperative leaders at different levels are blocking Bosnia's path to Europe, said Michael Steiner, deputy High Representative to Bosnia.

- Bosnian media are keeping up a petition campaign to retain Michael Steiner as deputy High Representative. Petitions will be sent to German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel a day before the Contact Group meets in Portugal this week.

- Mostar voters will be able to vote not only for Bosnian and Croat representatives in the Mostar city council but for representatives of other nationalities as well, said Edward Joseph, chief of the OSCE office in Mostar.
- Foreign Minister Jadranko Prlic said Bosnia is ready to establish diplomatic contacts with Yugoslavia with no additional conditions and in accordance with the Paris agreement.

- The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees announced the expansion of its bus service from Sarajevo to Serb-controlled Pale due to increasing demand from people who wish to cross the inter-entity boundary line. -- Sarajevo newsroom +387-71-663-384
